value.body: A two-year postgraduate programme in management. Universities award an MBA degree; AICTE-approved autonomous institutes award a PGDM diploma, and the two cover similar ground. The first year is general management, and in the second you choose a specialisation such as Finance, Marketing, HR, Operations, IT or Business Analytics.

items.label: Course length
items.note: Usually 4 semesters or 6 trimesters; 1-year executive programmes exist for experienced professionals

items.label: MBA students enrolled
items.note: All modes, including ~2.1 lakh in distance mode; PGDM institutes counted separately

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A bachelor's degree in any discipline (CAT asks for 50%, or 45% for SC/ST/PwD; final-year students can apply). Then an entrance test: CAT (IIMs and many others), XAT (XLRI and XAMI members), CMAT (NTA, AICTE-approved institutes), MAT (AIMA), or a state CET such as MAH-MBA CET, TS/AP ICET, KMAT or TANCET. Shortlisted candidates usually go through a written ability test, group discussion and/or personal interview.

value.title: At a glance
items: You do not need a commerce background — graduates from engineering, science and arts take the same tests.
Fees range very widely between government universities, IIMs and private institutes, so the cost has to be checked institute by institute.
Placement outcomes also vary a lot across institutes; published placement reports are worth reading closely.
Some institutes give weight to work experience, and many students work for a year or two before applying.
